key_insight: Perfumer uses an LLM-based agent to coordinate crystal relaxation and electronic band prediction, combining Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces first-principles workflow effort and reports a 2.75× overall relaxation speedup using learned pre-relaxation followed by Quantum ESPRESSO refinement.
method: Translate natural-language requests into structure-to-band workflows for uploaded structures or automatically constructed candidates.
Pre-relax structures with Perfumer-relax, then refine them with Quantum ESPRESSO.

Predict 12 band energies at requested wavevectors using a periodic graph neural network and latent Hermitian spectral head, preserving reciprocal-lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing a Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: Trained on 125,153 band structures, Perfumer-band achieved a median per-material MAE of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, with inference taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores.
watch_item: The reported median error does not establish worst-case reliability; predictions for unfamiliar chemistries or precision-sensitive applications warrant first-principles validation.
paper_title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
